Specifically, Global South countries interested in sharing, adapting and implementing zero hunger solutions from their peers will benefit from WFP’s enhanced support and from a deeper use of SSTC to achieve WFP goals to save lives and change lives.
WS1: Partnerships & ﬁnancing
WS2: Programme support & mainstreaming
WS3: SSTC results, learning & knowledge management
The policy will be implemented using a costed implementation plan for 2023-2027. It aims to: (a) consolidate what WFP does best in SSTC, (b) respond to emerging SSTC demands in critical areas, and (c) ensure quality and results in the SSTC WFP supports.
To this end and building up on specific provisions in the update policy, the costed implementation plan activates and accelerates corporate enablers (which are underlying capacities WFP needs to meet its current Strategic Plan) through the following six workstreams:
WS4: Strategic workforce planning
WS5: Communication & advocacy
WS6: Internal governance & coordination

Regional and country-level plans will be developed and costed based on each regional bureau’s and country office’s needs and priorities. Where demanded, the HQ SSTC Unit will provide support to develop these regional and where appropriate, country level plans. While ownership is shared by all corporate SSTC stakeholders and different units play an important role in putting the policy in practice, overall responsibility and accountability for policy implementation lies with the SSTC Unit.
